issues.body: The comment says the fuzz lane's randomized/replay legs are push- and schedule-driven, but deterministic corpus replay also runs on pull requests. The stable-toolchain coverage and compile-time seed linkage remain valid reasons for this regression test, so this is documentation accuracy rather than a correctness defect.
issues.fix_hint: State that randomized fuzzing is push/schedule driven while deterministic corpus replay also runs on pull requests, retaining the distinction that the fuzz lane needs nightly whereas this regression runs in the stable workspace test gate.
issues.title: Module comment still misstates corpus replay trigger coverage

verdict.summary: The path-ownership update correctly adds sparq-canon for its compile-time seed dependency, and the regression test is non-vacuous: it verifies five parsed input quads, four distinct input quads, four canonical output quads, and four distinct canonical output quads. The prior minor documentation issue remains unchanged: the module comment groups randomized fuzzing and deterministic replay as push- and schedule-driven even though the workflow also replays the corpus on pull requests. This does not undermine correctness, soundness, test validity, or security.
